This is all exactly right!

I'm sure you've heard the advice to noobs; "When you think buy, sell. When you think sell, buy"

The big guys here got lots of short orders hidden in the market (at each new high within the cp, they sold). Then they pushed price above the recent highs with great momentum. This freaked many weak sellers out, and had them close their shorts, creating long orders. This also excited breakout buyers (AKA complete noobs ) into buying - right into the edge of the zone, creating bucketloads of buy orders to fill their remaining shorts.

This is why, when trading CP, we should either await the first engulf, or know very well where the edge of the next zone is and plan the trade accordingly

This is how I see it all unfolding (from left to right following price and numbers on chart):

1) At this level we see only a small amount of candles in the base and also a large jump away of price. So we had way too many buy orders - price could not stay here for very long and moved away very fast. A sign that pro money has a stack of buy orders here.

2) Price moved up and pro money started taking profits - this shown by the candles with lots of wicks. Since they have open buy orders they need to counter trade with sell orders to exit their positions, this obviously sending the market back down from the highs.

3) All of this profit taking eventually sends price back down. Shown by big red candle.

4) That is the start of the compression. Big money knows they still have a stack of buy orders they need filled (at point 1) so they try and push price down to that level so they can get filled at the best possible price. At the same time they try and remove all resistance to price so that once it reaches 1 it can shoot back up without any supply to slow it down. So begins the slow process of taking out all the decision points on the way down.

5) Because of recent down trend caused by compression, many retail traders will try and follow the trend - "the trend is your friend" mentality. So they sell the continuation of the trend (sell orders placed at lower black line and stops at upper black line). These sell orders helps fill pro money buy orders - when retail sells pro takes their buys. Price also touched their stack of buy orders (from 1) and shot back up.

6) Their massive amount of buy orders at 1 pushed price higher. Once it broke the recent highs everyone who was short at 5 freaked out and exited their position (or got stopped out) creating even more buy orders which pushes price even higher.

7) Once price got back up to acceptable level pro money started taking profits again which sent price back down.

I'm not sure if this is right. Please try and pull this apart. I'd rather be wrong and learn something than people agreeing with me.

Here's my new take on it.

Trend followers would have had many orders sitting below that long wick. This is because if you look on the HTF H4 chart it is the bottom of a swing low during a recent down trend. Somewhere many people place trades for continuation of a trend.

But if you look left (on the HTF chart) it was also located at some significant demand.

So pro money wants to fill big buy orders at this level on last time (in the general demand area). Retail traders had many sell orders at this level (black line) so they compressed market down. They pushed it below the recent swing low (could that be the CPLQ?) to activate all the retail sell orders which they needed to fill their big buy orders. Once all the retail sell orders were absorbed price shot back up - this also stopped out many retail traders with sell orders creating even more buy orders sending price up with strong momentum.

I'm beginning to wonder if compression actually needs to visually take out every single decision point - but instead just give the general impression. Because we can't actually see where all the orders are sitting so there may actually be no decision points to take out in certain areas. Does that make sense?
